pages.scan: Top wide panel (clinic exterior, daylight, teal awning, glass door): caption top-left 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' A doctor in a white coat over a teal kurta with dark leggings and a stethoscope smiles and waves an elderly woman in a lilac sari (shoulder bag) inside. Two patients sit on metal chairs on the right, seen from behind. Lower-left panel (front desk): a receptionist in a blue print kurta with a long braid, on a corded phone and writing in a ledger beside stacked files, says 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' (left balloon) and then 'I wish everything were easier to manage!' (right balloon). Both tails point to her. She has a sweat drop and stress lines. Waiting patients fill the foreground from behind. Lower-right panel: the doctor stands with her hand at her chin, the receptionist still on the phone behind her, and says 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' Page number 1.
pages.observation: The order reads clearly: caption, then two receptionist balloons from left to right, then the doctor's reply in the right panel. Both receptionist balloons sit next to each other with tails to the same speaker, so they read as one continuous complaint. Nothing gets skipped. The receptionist is not named, here or later. The caption sits over the sky and wall and covers no faces. Lettering avoids faces and hands. The doctor's outfit (white coat, teal kurta, leggings, sandals, low bun) is the same in panels 1 and 3.

pages.scan: Top wide panel: caption top-left 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' and a teal label top-right 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. The doctor, seen over her shoulder, types on a laptop showing a setup form with steps. A sunset sky shows through the window and a coffee mug sits on the desk. Middle-left panel: the doctor, hand at chin, smiling at the laptop: 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' Middle-right panel: the receptionist stands holding a phone with a calendar app: 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' A teal label bottom-right reads 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. Bottom wide panel: the doctor at her desk with a laptop and the receptionist standing beside her holding the phone. A balloon between them with its tail to the doctor: 'One team. Better coordination.' Page number 2.
pages.observation: The order is clear from left to right and top to bottom: caption, label, doctor, receptionist with her label, doctor. The time jumps from daylight on page 1 to a sunset office with no time caption. 'Begins its onboarding' covers the change, but the shift to evening is only shown through the window. In the middle-right panel the 'WELBUK CARE' label covers the receptionist's lower dress and the edge of her left arm and hip, though not her phone hand or face. The top caption overlaps the top of the doctor's hair slightly. In the bottom panel the doctor's hair looks looser and her face younger and rounder than in panels 1 and 2. This is a mild identity drift. Because the bottom balloon sits between the two characters, a reader could briefly wonder who says 'One team', but the tail clearly points to the doctor.

pages.scan: Top-left panel: caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' An elderly man with glasses and a cane stands at the counter while the receptionist types. A QR kiosk stands at the far left. Top-right panel: caption 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' A young woman in a coral print kurta with a crossbody bag and wavy hair down taps a phone check-in outside the clinic entrance. Middle-left panel: caption 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' A bearded man in a sage-green shirt with a brown shoulder bag and a wristwatch scans a QR stand with his phone. The receptionist, the elderly man and the coral-kurta woman are visible in the background. Middle-right panel: caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' A close-up of Ravi's hands with a phone form and a check mark. Bottom wide panel: caption 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' A wall screen label reads 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12'. The elderly man, the coral-kurta woman and Ravi sit side by side in the waiting area. Page number 3.
pages.observation: The page is captions only, with no dialogue, and reads in a clear Z order. The 'A later morning' caption signals the time change from page 2's evening well. Ravi is introduced by name in a caption with no prior setup, which is acceptable. The caption says 'at the door', but the QR stand looks like it is inside, near the counter. This is minor. Continuity: in the top-right panel the coral-kurta woman wears her hair loose, but in the bottom panel she has a ponytail with a blue clip. This is a hairstyle mismatch within the same page. Ravi's shirt, bag and watch stay consistent. The slot labels A-10, A-11 and A-12 imply Ravi is A-12, which page 4 confirms, but that is inferred rather than stated. All captions sit in empty wall or sky and cover no faces or hands.

pages.scan: Top wide panel: caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' A screen label top-right reads 'NOW · A-12'. Ravi stands up from the waiting chairs with his bag on his shoulder, and the receptionist is at the desk on the right. Lower-left panel: caption 'A quick vitals check first.' A new character, a nurse in lavender scrubs with a lanyard and wavy shoulder-length hair, puts a blood pressure cuff on the seated Ravi (his bag on the floor) and says 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' Lower-right panel: caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' The doctor at her desk holds a tablet. A label on the tablet reads 'RAVI · READY' with a check icon. Page number 4.
pages.observation: The order is clear: top caption, then the screen label, the vitals caption, the nurse's balloon, and the right-panel caption and tablet label. The nurse appears without introduction. Her role is clear from her scrubs, so this is acceptable. The 'RAVI · READY' label breaks awkwardly after the middle dot ('RAVI ·' / 'READY') and covers most of the tablet screen. It sits close to, but not over, the doctor's hands. The doctor's outfit and hair match earlier pages. Ravi's bag and watch stay consistent from shoulder (panel 1) to floor (panel 2). No lettering covers faces.

pages.scan: Top wide panel (consultation room): the doctor gestures toward Ravi, who sits in an armchair with his bag beside him: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' A large teal label on the left over the desk and laptop reads 'PATIENT DETAILS: current vitals · prior health info · allergy panel · AI mic option · patient docs · lab reports'. Middle wide panel (long shot): the doctor asks 'May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?' and Ravi answers 'Yes, I agree.' A laptop between them shows mic and shield icons. A teal label on the right reads 'AI VOICE CONSENT: asked at the first visit, before any voice is saved'. Lower-left panel: Ravi, hand on his neck, says 'I've been feeling tired lately.' A teal label lower-left reads 'SOAP NOTES: fill in manually and choose ICD or SNOMED codes, or let AI listen and summarise the conversation' beside a laptop with a glowing mic icon. Lower-right panel: caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The doctor smiles warmly at Ravi, who is seen from behind. Page number 5.
pages.observation: The doctor's question 'Tell me what brings you in' in panel 1 is answered only in panel 3 ('I've been feeling tired lately'), after the consent exchange in panel 2 interrupts it. It still reads, but the answer is pushed back a panel. In panel 2 the 'Yes, I agree.' balloon sits right next to the doctor's balloon at the top centre, with a long diagonal tail down to Ravi on the far right. The consent label also sits directly above Ravi, so a reader may read the label before Ravi's reply or briefly take the short balloon as the doctor's. The tail does resolve it. The page has heavy text: three dense labels with jargon ('ICD or SNOMED codes', 'SOAP NOTES'). The panel 1 label covers the laptop and desk and comes close to the doctor's arm. The panel 3 label covers most of the laptop and sits right against Ravi's elbow. No faces are covered. Outfits stay consistent.

pages.scan: Top wide panel: a close-up of a laptop screen labelled 'SPECIALITY-SPECIFIC TREATMENT PLANNER', with three cards labelled 'Dentist: odontogram', 'Eye doctor: eye markers' and 'Paediatrician: growth scales · vaccines'. The doctor's hand (white coat cuff, teal sleeve) rests on the trackpad. Bottom wide panel: the doctor gestures toward Ravi and says 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' A teal label lower-left over the laptop reads 'PLAN OF CARE: intelligent prescribing · summary · drug interactions · labs · referrals'. Ravi sits smiling with his bag beside the chair. Page number 6.
pages.observation: The order is simple: the top screen labels from left to right, then the balloon, then the label. The top panel is a feature showcase (dentist, eye doctor, paediatrician) unrelated to Ravi, an adult who reports tiredness. It reads as an advertising aside rather than part of the visit, and nothing explains why the doctor is looking at these specialty tools. The 'Paediatrician' label runs past the screen onto the keyboard, and the three labels cover the lower part of each card illustration. In the bottom panel the label covers the laptop screen and the lower-left of the doctor's coat but not her face or hands. The doctor's line answers Ravi's 'tired lately' from page 5 adequately, though no diagnosis or next step is shown.

pages.scan: Top wide panel (front desk, waiting patients behind): the receptionist points at Ravi's phone as he leans on the counter: 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' Middle-left panel: Ravi holds up his phone showing an app with calendar and heart icons: 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' A teal label lower-left reads 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients'. Middle-right panel: the receptionist gestures, with Ravi's phone in the foreground: 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' Bottom wide panel: caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' Ravi walks away from the clinic waving, and the doctor and receptionist wave from the glass door. Page number 7.
pages.observation: The scene jumps from the consultation room on page 6 to the front desk with no transition. This is understandable as checkout but abrupt. The receptionist, Ravi, receptionist exchange reads naturally in order. However, 'Let's walk through what is available to you' is followed immediately by Ravi leaving, so the promised walkthrough is skipped and the line feels unanswered. In the middle-left panel the 'WELBUK HEALTH' label sits right against Ravi's left thumb and hand on the phone and covers the counter and monitor area, though not the phone screen or his face. The top-panel balloon sits close to the receptionist's face but does not cover it. Ravi's shirt, bag and watch stay consistent. The exterior matches page 1 (teal awning, glass door).

pages.scan: Top-left panel: caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' Ravi sits on a train by the window with a city skyline outside, holding his phone, bag on his lap, in the same sage-green shirt. Top-right panel: a label top-left reads 'WELBUK VISION'. An unnamed older grey-haired doctor in a grey coat gestures at a modern clinic, with small connected clinic icons in the sky. Caption: 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' Middle wide panel: a label 'WELBUK VISION' again, with caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' Ravi points at a tablet with profile icons and a heart, held by a woman in a yellow kurta, with a boy in an orange T-shirt beside them on a sofa. Bottom wide panel: the receptionist (holding a phone), the doctor and Ravi (waving, bag on shoulder) stand in front of the clinic. A label top-right reads 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and a caption bottom-left reads 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' Page number 8.
pages.observation: The page reads in order, but it leaves the story abruptly. 'Tomorrow' and 'us' create an unclear narrator and timeframe: whose hometown, is Ravi travelling, and is this the real future or a hypothetical? The older doctor and the woman and boy in the middle panel are new and unintroduced. A reader can guess they are Ravi's family, but nothing confirms it. The bottom panel returns to the clinic exterior without explaining when it takes place. Ravi wears the same outfit on the 'tomorrow' train as at the clinic, which may or may not be intended. The 'WELBUK VISION' label appears twice in a row. The separator style changes from '·' on earlier pages to '•' here. The bottom caption covers the receptionist's lower dress and feet and part of the doctor's lower legs. The top-right label covers part of the house-network illustration. No faces are covered.
